tts_summary:
Here is your midday market update for Tuesday, September 22nd.

The broad market is going essentially nowhere. The S&P 500 is flat, the Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, the Russell 2000 is up 30 basis points, and the Dow is down 43 basis points. Treasuries are flat across the curve. Crude oil is drifting slightly lower near $100 a barrel on hopes for a diplomatic resolution at the United Nations around Iran and the Middle East, and on news that Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline may be partially coming back online. Gold, silver, and bitcoin are all modestly in the red. The market is in a holding pattern — investors are waiting, watching, and positioning for what is shaping up to be a very dense catalyst window over the next ten days.

On the company side, AutoZone beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings with $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the quality of the beat is questionable — tariff refunds added 145 basis points to gross margins, a non-cash LIFO adjustment added another 105 basis points, and domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% versus the expected plus 3.1%. Management did say comp linearity was positive, and the stock is holding up.

MillerKnoll was a cleaner beat — 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and even stripping out the tariff refund tailwind the company still would have beaten at 42 cents. Guidance is mixed but the core result was solid.

THOR Industries missed on earnings — 78 cents versus 87 cents expected — with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year. Management pointed to a tough macro environment. Despite the miss, the stock is trading as an outperformer, suggesting expectations were already low.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive trial data for its GLP-1 obesity drug, showing 22% weight loss. That is a meaningful result in a very competitive space and is a positive catalyst for the stock.

Quest Diagnostics and Lab Corp are both getting hit hard after CMS released Medicare payment rates for lab services that came in worse than anticipated. This is a sector-wide reprice, not a company-specific issue.

On the AI side, Meta's Muse personal agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's Wednesday night keynote, and Shopify just announced it will allow Muse to complete purchases directly on its platform — a real distribution win. Amazon has blocked Muse, setting up an interesting competitive dynamic. Separately, Alibaba unveiled what it says is China's most powerful AI chip and hinted at training a model with up to ten trillion parameters.

Cognex is acquiring RealSense — a leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotics and physical AI — for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106 million. Strategic fit is clear but the price is not cheap.

Directionally, the market is waiting for its next move. The AI catalyst stack — Meta Connect Wednesday night, OpenAI's developer day on the 29th, and Micron earnings on the 30th — will likely set the tone for the next leg. Financials being broadly weak is worth watching. If banks, brokers, and asset managers cannot find footing, that is a headwind for the overall market. Stay focused on the AI names and watch energy — any progress on Hormuz could be a meaningful macro tailwind.
